title: Jeff Ulbrich, Tommy Rees & Craig Aukerman on taking on 6-0 San Francisco 49ers | Press Conference
text: Coach, you're getting ready to face perhaps the hottest quarterback in the league. Uh what are some of the things you all have to get lined up here for Sunday? >> Everything. Yeah, he's a great challenge. Um the more you watch him, the more you just appreciate the player that he is. Uh he does everything well. That's and that's the truth, you know, his his footwork, his getting through his progressions, his his timing. Um it's his accuracy, his the velocity he puts on the ball, the touch, the the and then when it's all said and done, the ability to create when it's not there, you know, um [snorts] sometimes you look at him and it's like you you underestimate the athlete that he is, but he's an exceptional athlete, you know, not not only the ability to evade and and run around, but break tackles. Like he has way more strength than you want him to have in the lower half. So, uh, this is going to be to date the biggest challenge that we faced by far from a complete offense. >> TV scouting on Monday, it looked like they kind of got off track when Evans went out. Does that affect uh what they do if he's not able to go? >> Well, you could tell like, and rightfully so, they they feature a lot of their passing game around number five, you know, and and his ability to to make the contested catch to to find the soft spots and zones and everything else in between. like he is a living walking hall of famer, you know, and there's no doubt about that. I don't think from anybody. There's no argument. So, um, and just historically speaking, like he plays with like everything, you know, so we are assuming he will play, you know, and and if he plays, then we're going to have to we're going to have to pay attention to him as you'd imagine. >> Is kiddo back, too? This is his uh he injuries and he's back out there. >> Yeah, we're we're anticipating them being fully loaded. You know, the the only one I would think that might be out is Debo Samuel. That's it. But [snorts] >> how much uh how much of what uh Raheem is doing out there uh as DC is kind of similar to what you guys are doing here? >> Uh it looks like, you know, and I haven't studied it as much as as you know, obviously Tommy has and the offensive staff has, but there is there's a lot of carryover from what they've done there because obviously they've had great success as a defense, you know, schematically. And then he's brought some some of the wrinkles that we've done here. Um, and he's done some more of the the front spacing that we've done. They've they've, you know, they were traditionally a four down team, you know, and they've been that for shoot since 2018, 17, whatever it is. So, there there there's some wrinkles for sure, but at the same time, like Raz, he's an exceptional coach, you know, and defensive mind. And in that, like he he also knows like I'm not going to screw this thing up. like they they have uh high level um just understanding of the defense that they they've had there since whatever 2019 really when when Solo got there and and instituted um the three deep stuff and some of the mixed principles some of the quarter stuff that we do. So they're playing at a high level too. So this is going to be a complete challenge for the entire team. In a situation like this, like how much do you because you know the other DC so well and that and that defense somewhat well, how much do you sit with Tommy and and do you guys talk during a week like this? >> A little bit. Yeah, a little bit. But at the same time, um they're going to know it better than I do by by game day and you know, they've they've studied on a on a deeper level. It's uh yeah, there's there there's always some things that you can you can share, but at the end of the day, like it's it's going to be uh >> yeah, it's a great challenge. It is. I won't get too deep into that. >> How did AJ look to you yesterday? >> He looked good. Like the the thing about AJ is like he's he's always going to try to play with whatever it is he's got. You know, he's got a a level of toughness, especially from, you know, the the corner position that that's pretty exceptional, you know. So, [snorts] he's going to his fight his butt off to be ready. Hopefully, he will be. We'll see though. You know, at the same time, um, you know, we're we're also not going to be irresponsible with him by any means because he's just he's so important to what we do going forward for the long run. >> At cornering in general, you guys have a lot of guys there now with AJ Avon, you know, Hughes Henderson could play it would appear as well. How do you kind of plan to blend that together? Would you run more dime? Would you like kind of how do you approach this weekend? Yeah, there is a part of my brain that goes there, you know. Um, but then we go through a game like the the previous one from an injury standpoint, it's like, man, I don't want to do any of that stuff just because you can get a little unhinged when you start creating these like one-off packages because the depth just is, I know it sounds like we have depth on paper, but when you start diluting it with a lot of dime and a lot of NASCAR and a lot of different packages, then, you know, sometimes that can become difficult when you to absorb an injury, you know. So, um, there'll be some stuff that we do, we always do, and we'll always have available to us, but, uh, um, maybe not as much as we normally would have in that way. >> What's a NASCAR package? >> It's just a combination of different rushers. It's trying to get your, you know, your fastest, you know, the the guys that you believe to be your best guys from a rush perspective up there. And then sometimes that can be a dime shell on the back end, you know. So, and we play with it both ways. >> Sorry, gosh. You've talked about this being a copycat league and Tommy Tommy does as well. I'm wondering how quickly that happens. Is it week to week? I mean, is it if a play has hurt you one week, you now expect it the next week or does it take some time to sort of work through the system? >> No, it's it it definitely week to week, you know, like whatever is on your tape is exactly how you're going to get attacked most likely. Um now what I would say about uh coach Shanahan which you know as we would all I think agree one of the best offensive minds in maybe in the history of football you know and in that like he is renowned for like how did you get beat okay cool I see a conflict there in rules or whatever it is he'll copycat how to beat you but it's not going to look the same >> not necessarily >> yeah like he'll find maybe a uh you know not necessarily a flaw but but as he might see it a flaw and maybe a a technique or a coverage or whatever it is and he's going to okay, there's conflict there that got him beat last week. All right, how can we create that same conflict maybe with a different window dressing formation motion concept, but at the same time beating you in a very similar way. So, um yeah, and that's that's him, but really that's every week like you better you better fix the problem. You know, for you to get beat on the same stuff from week to week like that's egregious. You know, you shouldn't do that. And conversely, you're doing the same thing, I would imagine, to the offenses that you face. You're going back one or two weeks. Is that, you know, in terms of how you study the opponent? Is that what's the where's the emphasis on that? Is that the first thing you look at? Is that where does that fall into your plan? >> Yeah, it's a little bit of everything, you know, when you try to attack an offense like there's a there's a scheme piece, you know, like take it take, you know, pressure for example. Like I'm going to look at the the protection system first, not necessarily just how they were beat, you know, and then we fold back another layer. Then it's personnel, like is there is there is there a guy? Is there an offensive lineman? Is there somebody that we want to attack in that way? Um and then for [snorts] sure a lot of that data gets, you know, it gets um accumulated through just studying opponents, you know, and and seeing how people have had success or lack thereof, you know, and stuff to stay away from is just as powerful as as how you're going to attack sometimes. Rick, correct me if if I'm wrong on this, but you know, I've heard Kyle's kind of offense is same plays and they kind of throw in a lot of different formations. Personnel packages, but they get to kind of their their same core stuff. When you're approaching that, [snorts] is it about like here's a buffet that we got to learn? We got to learn all these motions and formations and personnel and prepare for that, or is it kind of isolating it and saying however they get to it, here's here's kind of what we know their bread and is and we focus on on that. >> Yeah. And that's that's one of the major keys to victory this week. Like there is going to be to your point a million different types of window dressing formationally, motion, personnel. Um they're going to make it look, you know, 50 different ways, but at the the at the same time, like you said, it's going to be conceptually the same thing, the same concept, whether it be run, pass, whatever. And in that, like that's in my opinion his secret sauce because by repeating the same concepts with different window dressings, there can be a true emphasis on style of play, physicality, violence, finish, knockback. Um, and that's what shows up more so than anything on the tape, you know? So, like he tries to ultimately get you in your head and out of your heart, you know, and out of your fists and out, you know, all the things that we preach. He wants you thinking. He wants you slow. He wants you worried about adjustments as opposed to getting downhill and knocking the run back. So, it's finding that balance from a defensive perspective of doing enough to provide schematic solutions. So, we put our players in the best position to be successful, but at the same time, like guys, when the ball snap, you got to get ready to get downhill and go, you know, because um if they can run the ball 50 times, they will, you know. Is there a benefit then in kind of this attack style front where you take the thinking out of it. You say go execute, go play as fast as you can, especially against a very good offensive line there. >> For sure there is. Yeah, it's kind of the the foundation of it, you know, in a lot of ways. >> You completely comfortable with Kendall as the green dot at this point? >> I am. Yeah, I am. Uh I know that sounds crazy, especially for a, you know, fourth round rookie, whatever he is. you know, I think he's proven to be um one of the better communicators I've been around for a for a young player, for any player for that matter. He's uh he takes a lot of pride in getting everybody on the same page. Takes a lot of pride getting us in the right defense, making the right checks. Um just hearing him yesterday was uh it was just really cool. Even the pre- snap stuff, you know, just alerting everyone to some of the indicators that we had already had in the, you know, so um I'm excited for him to have this opportunity. It really, you know, and and and and at the same time like that's we're saying he's going to have the green dot, but I don't know if that's >> right. >> You know, I don't think that's >> it falls that way. >> Yeah, without a doubt. >> If it falls that way, you're comfortable. >> Yeah. Cuz at the same time, also, I know Divine and his nature is not to sit, you know, like if he can um he can respirate, he's typically going to try to get out there. So, you know, he's going to work his butt off to do so. Trent Williams still being able to play at such a high level at 38 >> makes no sense. I mean, he he will I don't think any will argue he's going to be one of the best [clears throat] left tackles in the history of this game, you know, and he's just a combination of everything. And it's amazing at 38. Like, I don't feel regression. [clears throat] I don't feel physical regression, speed, foot quickness. I don't feel any lack of urgency and physicality and toughness and nastiness. So, um, he's a great challenge, you know, and I pose that to the group of like, you know, like embrace that like this guy is a first ballot hall of famer and he will go down as one of the all-time greats. So, what an amazing opportunity. >> What's the advantage to having that like practicing against him every day when you're coaching somebody like CMC? >> It's huge. Yeah, it's huge. like what we we got to see every day of of training camp and OTAAS and mini camps and you know to get humbled in that way every day from a linebacker's perspective especially or a safety perspective whoever is responsible for them um it readies you for for games like this you know where um it's another guy that like the running back position you know historically you know you don't think of guys lasting a long time at that position just because there's so much physical toll put on them And uh gosh, 23 is is finding a way, you know, he's he's got the fountain of youth in some ways where like I don't see regression and in speed and um and obviously he's skilled at the highest level. And that's both as a receiver and as a runner. So, um, yeah, we're going to have to we're going to have to play really well, especially the guys that are matched up on on 23 cuz he's he's exceptional and they also they feature him in a lot of really unique ways that are challenging as well. >> With Avon, how how did he handle last week and what was kind of his heaviest snap count outside that corner? >> Yeah, like did it was uh he's another one that, you know, I feel so fortunate that our rookie class is built this way. like you sometimes tell a young guy like you're going to get an uptick or you're going to start or you're going to be featured or whatever it is. And you know like visual excitement but visual apprehension you typically see and feel from from younger guys and haven't felt that from any of our guys that have to have have had to step up from a rookie perspective like Avon. Um he's just going to keep getting better. You know the more turns the more as I I learn him. He's a guy that's got um the exceptional ability to just accumulate information and and and he's just he's a guy that just keeps stacking days and Kendall same as and Perkins same as and it's uh [snorts] it's it's fun to think about what these guys will look like in a couple years. >> Is this confidence or or swagger unique or rare for a 21-year-old >> Avon? >> Yeah. >> Yeah, it is. you know, especially playing that position because that's, you know, obviously you're you're going to get isolated a bunch. You're going to be put in harm's way a bunch and and you're going to go up against the best athletes, some of the best athletes on this earth. So, um, from that standpoint, like you got to be built to the right stuff. And it's as much mental and emotional as it is physical, you know, and and he checks all those boxes, you know, so his his future is bright. It is. >> Thanks, >> guys. when you went back and and watched last week and just not really running the ball as much as you did. Kind of agitated watching back and saying, "Man, I I really wish I called it more early on." >> Yeah, there's always calls you want back. Um, you know, we had two screens in the first two possessions trying to get be involved a little bit more outside of the box. Um, just how teams are defending us a little bit, trying to space it out. Um, yeah, there's always calls you want back. You know, I think, you know, we had some run success there on the third drive. got us in position, took a shot, then you're in, you know, get back on track and you're trying to cut it in half and call a run on third down, don't execute it. So, yeah, there's always plays you want back. The game script kind of flipped there late, but we know our identity. We know what where we've been good and we've played good offensive football. It starts with the run game and we're certainly aware of that. You know, we just um got to get back to our identity and get back to the things that we do really well. >> Have teams changed the way they play you? Because when Mike came back, you guys had I think it was 18 possessions week three, week four, and you scored on, I think 12 of them, might have been more. The last couple weeks haven't been as good. Have teams change the way they're playing you guys, do you think? >> Uh, yeah, we've definitely gotten some things that um vary from their identity of what they've shown on film. You know, obviously, you look at the pressure rate we got last week. you look at um kind of more loaded fronts the last two weeks which is a big departure from Baltimore who they were bottom line is we have to execute and I have to do the a better job making sure we put our players in position to execute you know teams are going to have answers we have great counters for that we have plays that we can either get to we have plays that we can execute you know we got a score in the red zone a couple weeks ago we got to convert on third down last week and put ourselves in better position on first and second and um we're all committed to that you know we have a plan moving forward to make sure that if teams do vary from what they've shown, we'll have answers and we got to continue to highlight our best players. >> Talk about being a cop being a copycat league. How quickly does does that copy take place? >> Well, pretty quick from one week to the other here. Yeah, it does. I mean, I think teams see it. Um, look, we played really well for two weeks on offense, right? And uh teams were going to have answers. You know, number seven um surely dictates some answers from other defenses to have a plan for him. And um we just I got to do a better job of getting those to our you know um compliments off of that quicker. >> So but but not even necessarily pertaining to these last couple of weeks, but in general when you're game planning, you expect something that hurt you one week to immediately show up the next even if they've never sh even if whoever has never shown. Yeah, I think it's a great question because it's what we go through obviously during the week of hey, it might not be part of what they do, but what is most similar to what they do that could appear the same way, right? It's kind of you have to take what's worked against you, apply it to how a team maybe has their plan or their package, >> try to project what they might be >> correct. Yeah. Yeah. That's that's dead on. Yeah. I mean, that's a that's part of this league. That's part of each week. That's a great challenge. um similar to how defense has got to react to how an offense might attack a certain structure of defense and um but that's what makes this league fun and that's what makes the challenge each week great regardless of who you're playing. >> Tommy, you mentioned kind of first and second down and getting more into a third and manageable goal. Been your evaluation of of the group there and then how much are you focused this week on on kind of >> Yeah, last week really last two weeks, you know, we we were lucky not lucky we executed on third and long two weeks ago which kept us driving and then we didn't score in the red zone. You know, last week we did not have great success early down. Um it's such a key because you keep a team off balance. You keep a team um unsure of what's coming after that. When you're ahead of the sticks, it opens up so much more of the uh the call sheet. So um our early down success had been pretty good. Um and then obviously we got to be better there. And look, I I put that on my shoulders. I told the group on Monday, you know, us starting slow, us having drives that stall out early in the game, early in a in a drive, that's on me. It's not on them. I got to put them in the right position to have success and um you know that's something that I feel very strongly about. And how difficult, you know, as a play caller, like when when you find yourself down a couple of scores early and you know, hey, our our bread and butter is kind of the run game and what we can then do off of that, like how do you balance wanting to continue to lean on that, but >> yeah, [sighs] it's hard, especially as the game gets late, but um you can't abandon your identity. You know, I think, you know, starting there in the third quarter, they came out pressuring. We had a chance, you know, we had a PI on Drake and then, um, you know, we had a chance to run it there after the penalty. we didn't get many yards and bless you and then we you know try to continue on from there but you got to find other ways to get your best players you know involved. You got to find ways to highlight what you do well and then there comes a certain point where the clock and the score doesn't doesn't match up and you have to play a certain style which certainly you know we face there for for about a quarter. Um, so again, if we're if we're if I'm doing a better job early in the game, early in the drives, you know, all those take care of themselves. And look, I think we've shown we've not been shy to give Bejon the ball. And and we got to continue to find ways to have success doing so. Find ways to keep teams off balance, find ways to um, you know, make sure that we're operating at a high level. >> And why did the really wide wide receiver splits not work at this level? >> Why do they not? Yeah. >> I think the speed of the game. >> Yeah. I think the speed of the players and the speed out there is a little different. I think the hashes matter a little bit like college to NFL. >> Um like you're talking like the tennesses of the world. Yeah. >> I just hear you can't do that in the NFL and I just don't understand why. >> Yeah. I mean I do think the field dimension affects it and then I think the speed of the opposition it's a different level. You know, you got better guys in space on both sides, but certainly defensively they there's not as many holes to attack. Tommy, I've heard that um you know, bringing extra pressure can be a way to keep a running back in as a pass protector. As you're looking at, you know, more of these pressure fronts and and things like that, do you think that's a part of it from these defenses is wanting to keep number seven in the pocket as opposed to out? >> Yeah, we need to execute against the pressure. You know, I got to do a better job of giving solutions against the pressure to to have answers. If you know, we said to the guys, if you know, they're going to see that on film and we got to we got to correct it. We got to have answers. We got to make sure that we're operating at a high level when pressure does does happen. Yeah, they can blitz bean, keep him in the in the core and make sure that he's not out in space. You know, we've had some opportunities outside of that to get him out there against pressure looks, but um you know, again, it falls on my shoulders. We got to do the best job we can coaches um to put our players in position to have success and then make sure that the details within our protection uh system are sound. >> Flip it over to San Francisco. What do you see from that unit? Yeah, they do a great job, man. They're flying around. Um, you know, obviously [clears throat] the middle linebacker kind of makes everything go for them. Um, they play great team football, play great team defense. Um, you know, I think they're first or second in the league in limiting explosives. They rally to the football. They populate the ball. When a ball gets in space, you see seven, eight guys around it. Their D line is up the field, plays hard. those safeties come downhill and are really aggressive which um you know as just a football fan it's like it's great to see you know safeties playing that way obviously not against us but um I think you know Rahee's done a great job with that group and they've done a nice job of having some variables that are probably different than who they've been in the past and they're getting their D line to play really well without Bosa um you know obviously they're they're clicking right now so it's a great challenge for us they do a good job scheme but the style they play in is what when you turn on a film and you want to compliment a team, you see that when you when you watch their film. >> How important is Kyle's rack ability? It's >> huge. Yeah, it's huge. Um, you know, I think he's the at his best when he has the ball in his hand in open space. And so, um, you know, Kyle's shown that throughout his entire career. He's certainly shown that over the last few weeks. And, um, again, it's our job to put him in position to have those plays. >> How happy were you with the way that he I don't know what he ended up with last week, but the last quarter he kind of got rolling. How how happy about that were you to kind of see him really get going? >> There wasn't a lot of happiness on Sunday for me if you want to be be completely honest. Um I'm happy for Kyle because of the work he's put in, the patience he's had to get him going. Um for us to reach our full potential, he's got to be a big part of that. And um you know, for him to kind of stay the course and have success, obviously we want that for him. Um but again, happiness on Sunday was was hard to find for me. So, >> did you play much Madden as a kid? Were you a big Madden player? >> Um, your normal amount, I would say. I mean, maybe above normal, but yeah, I like Madden. >> You think that there was Was there any carryover? Did it Did you learn it? >> This is Kev's Kev's talked about this, right? >> Yeah. Last week. >> Yeah. Kev, that's his big deal. Like, if you've called plays in Madden, you've called plays. I mean, yeah, you have to you have to think >> you you were on the other side of that argument. It feels like >> No, no, no. I'm good. I'm good. I just it's funny that you brought up the Madden thing because Kev obviously talks about it. Um yeah, I mean you have to think critically about what you want to do and so I think for all of us that grew up playing I agree with Kevin on this like if you grew up playing Madden you've had to put yourself in position um to think things through. Um it's probably a little easier in Madden I [laughter] think you know but than it is >> so but uh yeah of course played those growing up. Do you think that the young you were talking about young offensive coordinators last week? Is there any carryover to more guys being ready at a young age because of that? Is that any factor at all, do you think? Because this is sort of you're sort of that Madden generation. >> I mean, I I don't know if I'm qualified to draw that that parallel, you know, like I just >> look, I played Madden because I like playing Madden. I like football. >> I'm sitting here today. Probably somewhere there's a correlation, you know, somewhere. Um, but yeah, it's hard for me to draw that direct parallel. >> We had John yesterday. >> We had Van yesterday and he said in a game he run it about 50 times. Um, when you go into like a game, is that something that like maybe you think of go to your guys like what do you want to do in these situations? >> Um, I I expect all competitors to want the ball. You know, I think for Be um look, he's he's a great special player and I got to do um the best job I can to make sure that we feature him to impact the game. Um you know, Bee's as good of a teammate, as good of a person as you'll find. So, as a competitor, I expect him to want the ball, but he's also the first guy to to understand that whatever job is asked of him, he's gonna do to his fullest capability. So yeah, I mean, look, we have a lot of work during the week of talking to our players, discussing what we're doing. There's nuance things that we we consistently go through and um >> yeah, no, I'm I'm I want him to touch the ball 50 times, too. So, >> it uh it looks like 49ers have kind of improved as the season's gone along against the run to that point. What have you seen from them in the growth in that area? >> Yeah, I think their front does a great job. I mean, they're they're an attack style front. They get vertical on on blocks. their linebackers. They have two really good linebackers. Their nickel is um damn good against the run. He's aggressive. Um you know, he's able to blitz, shoot gaps. You know, he does a good job with matchups on receivers and then those safeties are downhill. So, like you look at the middle part of their defense and they have really good players that are physical and aggressive and committed to stopping the run and then their line is penetrating. So, um they're able to free up some of the the hits for those guys on the second level. And um again, they just they swarm the football. You turn on the film and it's for somebody that played Madden or likes football like you you see a defense being played the way that you appreciate and it's a lot of credit to again Raheem and that group and the way they've built the culture there and um they've done a really nice job. >> Cool. >> Thank you guys. with Zachariah from last weekend. What do you think happened on the punt the return as well? And then where's your confidence level in him now? >> Yeah. Well, first off, the confidence level is still extremely high for Zachariah. Like we love his skill set. We love how he goes out to work every single day. You know, he works hard. He wants to be great at it. So, you know, the level of confidence is extremely high with him as, you know, and he'll continue to do that because we know how he wants to work. So, you know, the biggest thing, you know, him going out there muffing the punt. Uh, is we just got to get back to the basics with him. Um, let him know that, hey, again, it starts with the confidence. Got to let him know all the different types of kicks that people end up kicking. They end up kicking a banana ball with that. Uh, just understanding that, hey, the technique-wise, we got to take one more step to come up there and catch that. If you don't feel comfortable, we just got to get away from it. Let everyone know that we're not going to go and field that punt. Um, and then you know the one with the ball security issue, that's that's just a big thing that we'll continue to harp with him. Ball security is at an elite level every single time. It has to be. Uh, we can't put the ball on the ground on special teams at any point in time. >> When you have a, you know, a young guy like him in that moment when he's really down on himself and all that, how do you walk the line between hard coaching, but also trying to make sure you're not crushing him either? >> Yeah, definitely. It's it's one of those things as a coach you got to really handle. And you know, my biggest thing of going over there and just talking to them, I I I want to be the first one, you know, let them know that, hey, we still got a bunch of confidence in you. This whole team has has confidence in you. Uh we want you to go back out there again the next punt or the next kickoff return, whatever it is, we want you to be the guy back out there and just let them know that, hey, it's it's good. We just got to make make sure we get back to the basics of everything that we do. What have you uh seen from San Francisco special teams? >> Yeah, really good. I think Brent Ber does an excellent job there in San Francisco. Even when he was with the Jets, like I I've have a lot of respect for him. They do a really good job. I think their punter is having a great year right now. Uh left- footed punter, which for Zachariah will be different. uh we'll we'll end up really talking to him about the different spin of the football, you know, because it is different versus a right and left footed punter on how, you know, if he hits a traditional punt and it's a spiral and it turns over, it's going to go deeper and going to drift to our right. If it doesn't turn over, it's going to go short and to our left. So, those are the things that we'll continue to talk about, but their punter is having a really good year. I think they're in the top 10 of net punt. They do a really good job with coverage. uh whether it's their gunners with number 33 Neil or their interior players, they do a really good job. Uh their kickers doing a really good job as well as far as kickoffs is concerned and then their kickoff return team was really good in 25. Again, they they do a really good job creating angles and different types of spaces for those guys to go. So, we got our hands full. They're a good team. >> Is there a way to practice a lefty spin? >> Oh, yeah. Yeah. Our our equipment guys are unbelievable. They change the jugs. And that's where you see Oz a little bit more for us uh back there. That the one Zachariah was still more of a field punt. Yeah, I think when you study it, um, you know, in college you see more of the 10 yard line, the punters are so good in the NFL that, you know, I I even tell Jake inside the 20 yardd line on plus 50.
