Why didn't somebody pick this off?" But it gets there. I mean, does anybody Is that something that is just different than anyone you've ever seen? >> Yeah. Uh, his ability to see the field um is second to none, you know? So, just being able to see space and having an understanding of how things are going to develop um the coverage we're getting within the routes and how that can that may dictate where people are on the field. Um and then yeah, he can he can make all those throws. >> When when you go through the film, I guess I'm not sure about giving anything away, but uh how do your coaching points change knowing that the way defenses are playing you guys are different because of the way that they're respecting the running game more? Um, at the end of the day, it's still we got to be efficient on first, second down. Um, so we talk about that. Again, getting the run game going is going to be important. Um, you want to generate explosives. Uh, so if they're there, take those. If not, check it down. We got great weapons. Uh, whether it's out of the back field, whether it's tight end position, it's underneath people that we have. Like, if the shot's not there, check it down. Stay efficient. Keep the chains moving. So, um, that's really playing that game, you know, and and knowing that if things don't go great initially, like we can still, uh, on the second, like get back into the third and manageable or even pick up the first down on a second long, but staying efficient and knowing that, uh, that run game can help us be that as well. Last one >> on that run game. Um, you mentioned under center and all that stuff and having Kenneth here. I think last year Matt used to call them breather runs. You know, how many more just straight breather run type plays are there in a game this year compared to last year with the addition? >> Yeah. Um, I don't have an exact number for you, but definitely, you know, you can tell that's been an uptick for sure um with the under center stuff and um there could be some alerts and kills to that. You know, we also have the gun RPO things that we do. Um, but there's definitely been uh an increase of hand and letting those guys go to work. >> Yep. Thank you. Hey, hey, hey. Go ahead for Chris. >> What are the biggest challenges that Seattle poses for you guys heading up there on some of that football action? >> Um their scheme runs and uh I think Sam Dorno has played really really great ball in that schematic. Um have a really good running back. Unfortunately the rookie got hurt, but have a really good system um of how they scheme up plays and have one of the best receivers in the league. Jacob, >> I asked Spags about the interaction. I don't know if you've seen it that you and Joe Cole had on the sidelines during the game the other day and looked like he put his hand on your shoulder and you were like kind of No. Uh and but Spec said which one for the altercation? Is it just that you and Joe have that kind of relationship? Yeah, I think um you know just the passion of wanting to win, wanting to succeed, and wanting to be great and push each other beyond measures. I think that's that's what you got right there. >> That happen with other people too on the sidelines just get emotional and >> Oh, no. I'm We're Me and Joe are pretty emotional and pretty competitive. So, I think it's more so about pushing the best out of each other. It's a push pull technique. push each other and pull each other together together at the end of the game. >> Christ, you just evaluate how your performance so far this season, what you've seen coming off film. >> There's room for progression. Uh I think so far um it's uh it's about getting better every game. Um haven't reached my sag number. I think I got a point five over sack right now. It's all good. It's not how you start, it's how you finish. So just continue to progress game in and game out. And at the at the end of the year, it tells your story. It kind of tells your journey. Um where you at at the end of the year. So for me, it's about a climb, the the climb of the journey. Um you know, the season has what four quarters, 16 games, 17 games, four quarters in and a penny. So you know, when you think of it in that aspect of it and you break it down in that schematic, I think you can take a lot from each quarter. you know, how did I do the first four games, the second four games, you know, did I build, did I get better? What areas of improvement? And then at the end of the year, it tells your journey. So, I think right now it's about improving. Um, the sacks will come. Um, that's that's where my focus is at. >> Chris, did the buy you have no control as to when the buy is, but did the buy come at a at a right time for you saying that you were limited with the calf? How much was the calf sort of giving you some discomfort? And do you feel much better now having that additional week to sort of get right? >> Feel really good coming off a by week. You know, extra week of work is off of work is always uh beneficial, especially when you're dealing with little necks like that. Um preferably rather by being like week eight, 8 through 10 somewhere around there where our bodies are really beat up. But I'm very fortunate that it came early as it did and you know it gave me an extra week of rest. >> We've uh been trying to it's a moving target on roughing the passer. When you went back and watched looked like probably you earned yours. Um Ashton's was a little closer. Are you guys been doing this a long time? Are you totally set on what it is anymore? >> I want to say I earned it. Uh like I got an appeal coming of you know just say I just did this. It's crazy. Uh, you know, I um I grabbed him and I landed on the side and I I just hope that the league can see that I tried to land on the side. Maybe I was a second late, but they say two steps and then clearance. So, you know, we we're going to look at the film and analyze that. And, you know, you take Ashton's where, you know, he stopped in a quarterback flop. I think the next progression of that is when you make those type of calls and being able to go look at the look at the film as a ref and to be able to pull that flag back up when you see that there's flopping going on. You know, the NBA came up with a rule for flopping. They find the opposing player for flopping. So, some something on those bases, but you know, you don't argue with the ref calls. you just, you know, try to address it after sending it into the league and, you know, let them do their due diligence on um whether it should have been called or not. >> How are you, how does that appeal process work? Do you do you get a chance to get on the phone with them or Zoom call and kind of plead your case? How does it work? Yeah, I mean, you know, the arbitrator usually asks you what were you thinking and um you know, um you talk through the mechanics of the play. Um whether it was good or bad and you know how you perceive the play in your head, especially when you going full speed, you know, cuz things are different when you slow them down other than when you run at 100 miles per hour. So, you know, in that in that case, I think I was moving too fast for myself and I grabbed him and uh I was just trying to bring him down and there's a two-step rule that the league has said that quarterback in the pocket two steps, you know, but so hopefully I can uphill this and show the league in good grace that it's nothing is never intentional with me. I'm not a dirty player. >> Is is the arbitrator a former player or is it just a >> um John Ryan? John Ryan. So, you know, that that doesn't mean he um that doesn't mean he favors the player, but he he he he's a middleman of doing what's right and uh you know, someone you can trust in to make sure that they get the call correct. >> Have you ever appealed before? Have you ever won one? >> I've been very um fortunate in my my 11 year span of been able to appeal and get fines rescended. So, you know, hopefully this is another one under my belt. >> Two more. Go ahead, Matt. Go ahead. Chris, you played for with three years with Allan Bailey. What do you remember about him and any any good stories from Alan? >> Man, just a great guy and you know, his his family his family and loved ones is in my prayers. You know, very unfortunate situation. You know, I I was I was able to spend four years with Alan Bailey and he was Mike Vet along with Dun Terry Poe and Jay Howard and they kind of taught me the necessities of being a pro and how to approach the game um professionally and um you know to hear the devastating news yesterday kind of broke my heart um crushed me. Um, Alan Bailey was not only um a a teammate, he eventually transitioned to a friend and you know um outside of work, we started to establish a friendship and communication and you know and those unfortunate situations you you never can expect and and you never wish that upon anyone especially a close friend like Alen Bailey such a nice guy you know they will welcome me with open arms taught me the way without even me having to as showed me how to be a pro and um his family is in my prayers. >> Uh Chris, we've seen it in baseball where guys are allowed to challenge a call in the strike zone. Would you be in favor of something like that for defensive pass interference or for roughing the passer where you could have the ability to enact a review? >> I mean, I would be in favor of it if it doesn't affect the challenges we have because I think right now we have two challenges, right? and and then you lose that you you you lose one and then you have one left and then under two minutes is the the ref has to view the call, >> So if they're willing to add a challenge f flag or not go against two challenge flags, I think it's reasonable, but more so I feel like put it in the ref's hand. um rough and the passer or pass interference are calls that can be reviewed by the ref and be corrected upon hand instead of I think a couple years back when we had the challenge flag and everyone start challenging pass interference where it became a bigger deal than the league expected instead of making it a distraction games end up being held longer than you know because everybody was throwing challenge flag they was challenging every PI call I think it's more so put it in the ref's hand and allow the refs to kind of review the call on calls as of defensive pass interference, offensive pass interference or roughing the passer because there's a lot of times though calls look different when it's full speed. You know what I mean? >> Thank you guys.

title: Head Coach Dan Campbell previews Lions vs Packers | 2026 Week 7 Opponent Preview
text: Joined now by head coach Dan Campbell as we get ready for our week seven opponent preview against the Green Bay Packers back at home. When you're trying to maintain consistency coming off a dominant win against Arizona, what's the focus for this team this week? >> Well, I think the focus is getting back [clears throat] to work. We got to restart this engine, you know, that's the guys have had some time off um and so it's really let's get going again. Green Bay, they're still rolling now and they're playing their best football. We got to start the engine back up and let's build on what we did at Arizona. >> Start the engine back up with quarterback Jordan Love who has just done things really well in the passing game, but we see here on this play where he can beat you with his legs. How do you contain him here? >> It's not an easy task. The guy is really playing at a high level and he's very difficult to defend. Right, they just throw this in there. They've got it every once in a while, the good old read run, you know, and that's why because they'll just lull you to sleep. They'll do some of this gun RPO handoff handoff and then all of a sudden they'll read one of these in a critical and he's a good enough athlete and can run well enough to where you know, there's 12 yards in a first down. So, he's dangerous that way, man, with his legs, with his arms, his his mind, the whole thing. >> High rate in the passing game. He leads the NFL with 988 passing yards on downfield throws and he hits one of his targets here in Christian Watson. What makes him so elite in his route running ability? >> Well, what you know, Watson is really his game is really improved throughout the years. He's done a good job. He's much more crafty, much more precise. You know, he was raw when he came in, but he just continued to work and these guys he's got a tremendous amount of trust for this guy cuz he knows where he's going to be and he does it with speed and now he's got finishing speed here. Look, that takes a lot of trust to be able to rip it and know your guy is going to be there and they got a really good rapport together, but this guy and Golden are dangerous, man. They can just take the top off your whole defense and make plays on the ball. >> Josh Jacobs is expected to be back. We know he hasn't played this year, but how does he change the picture in the run game for them as that's been a struggle for them to start the season? >> Look, anytime you get a really good player back. Look, I I like all those backs in Green Bay. I think they run hard, they do a good job. This guy's just different. He He has played in this league a while. He's dangerous out of the backfield, but he's a power runner, man. He's got vision. This is a really good example of Look what he does. He just pulls this right to the double team. He knows this hole's back here. He's going to make you declare what you're going to do, and then he finds it, and there goes the burst. And once he goes downhill, he's heavy, he can see it, he can feel it, he's got enough speed to take it all the way. If he's playing, which I'm assuming he's playing, we can't let him get going. >> Absolutely. Going to the other side of the ball, new defensive system there from Arizona's former head coach Jonathan Gannon. He's their new defensive coordinator. A lot of three safety looks, including Xavier McKinney, who has just been a force defensively for them. He's so good at confusing quarterback reads. How do we see that on this interception? >> This guy, though, he's a pro, man. He knows how to disguise. He He'll show one look, give you another look, man, bait the quarterback. He just plays very disciplined type of game, and then he's got these instincts to make these breaks, man. He sees it all the way, and here he goes. And he He's a good player, man. That was a great pickup by them 2 years ago, cuz he's been a thorn in our side. So, he's dangerous, man. He can do everything for them. >> I think there's a reason why this team leads the league in interceptions. They're doing a lot of things well on defense. How do you beat them Sunday? >> You don't throw the ball to them, and you [laughter] and you don't fumble it to them. That Let's start there. Um they've done a good job with that. Man, you got to You have to be poised. The last two games they're playing at a high level is because they're creating enough chaos to where these teams are making errors, and you can't do that, man. You got to just calm yourself down. Doesn't mean you'll be perfect. Trust what you've been given. Trust that you can Your guy's going to take care of any pressure that we've got. You're going to find the ball. Goff's going to make the right decision. Catch, tuck, knife, and let's get to the next play. >> And it helps when you've got a quarterback who is playing at their best right now. No interceptions through week five, the only quarterback to be in that category. How have you seen him elevate his game this year? >> Yeah, he just continues to grow, you know? He he's This guy has played enough football now to where he's seen a little bit of everything and nothing really fazes him. It just doesn't, you know. He's good that way and you know, you can hit him, you can do some things early. He'll always settle in, calm down. When you've got a guy that's playing at a high level like he is, you ask him to do a lot. You put a lot in it cuz you can trust that he's going to take care of the football for you. He's going to take the shots through there. If not, he'll just check it down one more time to LaPorter or Gibbs or Saint or let them go to work. We'll find our place. >> Awesome. Thanks, coach. Good luck this weekend. >> Thank you. Appreciate it.

title: Detroit Lions Coordinators meet with the media | October 22, 2026
text: You look at them second in punt return. I think averaging over 15. I think they're ninth in kickoff return. Just what makes them so good in in [clears throat] those areas. Is it one of the better units you guys have faced in terms of the stress on your coverage units? >> Yeah, these guys do a great job. Uh they got good players. They're playing well. They play hard. Um I mean honestly, Green Bay has been like that for us for a lot of years. They do a good job. They got a lot of big guys, big physical players. Um so in the return game, we got a great challenge for us, great matchup. Um I know our guys are excited about it. But I'm excited about it. But, uh, I do have a lot of respect for them, uh, their organization, what they've done over the years, uh, how their guys play on special teams, and, uh, it'll be a good challenge for us. >> Got a, um, return man situation to kind of sift through with, uh, after losing Tom, brought in Carter. I'm just curious like how how open is that competition this week? What are you kind of looking for for somebody to emerge both on the punt and kickoff? >> I think uh, um, I don't know that it's like totally open. And I mean, I think DeAndre Carter's got a lot of experience. He'll probably step in and return punts for us um and kickoffs for us in the game along with um Sailors um and we'll just keep going as it's been. Obviously, Levit factors in to some degree. Um Lucky Jackson's had some experience doing it a little bit. None of those guys the same type of experience that DeAndre had. >> Beyond the experience, what do you what do you like about him? What does he bring to this? >> Uh he's uh well, you know, obviously we don't know a ton um in terms of like how he is today, but uh I know how he is firsthand. In 2018, he joined [clears throat] us. I think he had gotten cut by like four teams. Um and uh he had bounced around. He kept on fighting trying to make it. I think we were in week four or something like that. I believe it was when Darren Sprouls went down. And then he came in, we were playing against Tennessee. And uh you know, he did what he does. He catches the ball. He competes. He gets downhill, he's quick, um very competitive. I mean, his story is like the ultimate story of just overcoming all the obstacles and he plays the game that way. Um he loves playing football. I've always respected his game. I actually didn't even bring him up. Our pro personnel guys had him on the list of a couple guys that we looked at and worked out and uh so anyway, I know a lot about him. Um and I think he'll do a great job for us. by week is obviously kind of uh famous for like a self scout week and stuff like that. Like what what do you like about your new sport? >> Yeah, I I say this every every year I think after the by-week, but to me like the the old days of football was self scout during the by-week. Like modern football, I mean, you're self scouting yourself after every play. Um really, and I and I really mean that. Um but certainly every week. I mean, all of our self scout is done at the end of every week. So, it's all up to date after each game. Um, but you have more time to look at yourself, look at league trends, maybe spend more time on that stuff. Um, you know, I think the biggest thing you can do is look at yourself. It's one thing to want to be like somebody else, but the most important team we have is our team. Um, I always say to the players, and it's going to be about how we play the plays. And so, it's nothing different though than any week. I mean, we're trying to improve. You know, I always say that our our goal as a football team or a unit on special teams is to improve week in and week out and get a little bit better each week and play our best football at the end of the season. Um, and not look at any one player, any one game, but look at it in ter in terms of just getting better um better every day, better every week, getting better throughout the course of the season. And if we do that, we'll be playing great football at the end of the year. There's going to be some ups and downs along the way, but I [snorts] think our guys have done a good job so far. We've played hard. Um, but we got a long way to go and a bunch of really good teams to play against. >> Are there any uh trends around the league that that particularly interests you? >> No, nothing nothing uh crazy. Um, again, I don't get too involved with that, but I I definitely pay attention like is there something that's hot that everybody's starting to do that we're going to see your face? Um, and is there something you like that might apply to you or how could you incorporate some ideas, but nothing nothing too outside the box or in particular? >> Hey Dave, Jack Fox's last punt of that Cardinals game might have been his his best of the season. Just how would you evaluate his his performance so far this year? >> Yeah, he's had a great year. Um, you know, he's a he's been a great player for us ever since I've gotten here. Um, and truth be told, he was a great player the year before I got here um in his first year. So, he he's done he's done the same thing he's always done. To be honest with you, I do think he's improved in some areas. He's better directional control than he's been throughout his time here. I think he's improved in the uh situational plays as we're getting down into the 50 yard line, some of that type of stuff. Uh his holding certainly improved throughout the years. Um [clears throat] but a great player, a great weapon. Obviously, he's got a lot of things he can do. Punt the ball, throw the ball, all that stuff's a factor. Um, so anyways, yeah, great player. Um, he's playing well. He obviously can improve still also just like we all can, just like I can. But, uh, we're fortunate to have him. I know that. >> I don't know if it's a trend, but one thing that's popped up is there's been a couple games that have been decided like, you know, a team scores with less than 10 seconds to go and the other team, be it with a kick return or or, you know, playing for that long kickoff. Uh, you know, one play kicks a field goal. Do [clears throat] you What is the cut off? like how how much time does a kick return take? When do you >> Yeah. No, it's a it's a valid uh it's a valid question obviously that's come up here. Something we talk about all the time. I think there's a lot of things to it. Number one, if you if you tackle the guy and you win the game, well then you you made the right call. If the guy hits a big return, well then maybe you should have kicked in the end zone, let the defense play. It's one of those things that in this game you could argue every which way after the fact. Uh I say in the NFL, you can't win if you lose. Um and if you lose, you probably win a lot of things. It's like no one looks at the team that won the game but missed the field goal early in the game. I think Kansas City two weeks ago or something like that or um two weeks ago they missed a kick and they end up winning the game with field goal kick and so you know he's a hero but if they miss that one lose the game it was because of that. Um anyway it's never because of one play. Um but uh yeah I think uh kickoff roughly takes 5 seconds. So if you're 5 seconds or left or less and you think you can go down there and stop a guy, then kicking the ball to him is probably a good idea. But then you also get into the argument of, okay, well there's 7 seconds. If you kick a touchback, how many plays can they get in 7 seconds? Maybe they can get two plays in there. Is that enough time for them to get a chunk? Get down. If they have a timeout, not have a timeout factors into it, obviously. So there's a lot that goes into it. I think some of it's got to be, you know, who's your coverage team? Who's their returner? How much time's in the game? What's the score? Do they need a field goal? Um, who's their kicker? Are you outside in the wind and weather? Are they kicking in the wind? Are they kicking with the wind? Like all of it probably factors into it. I think that that scale slides. And I think we saw that with Jacksonville and Philadelphia or whatever and some of these games here. But uh ultimately the head coach got to make a calculated decision based on those variables which are things we think about and talk about going into the game and then it's going to come down to his decision. But ultimately it really comes down to whichever side of the ball is out there executing. And I I say that all the time like people in the analytics world they act like the defense can't play or can't stop them. So it's like well if we gave the ball they would have scored. Well there's a thing is stopping them too. Um so you can give them the ball back and stop them. Um or you can kick off and stop them on the kickoff. So like in the old days they say kick the touchback. Why why' they kick it to the return? They should have kick a touchback. Well, there's a thing is kicking off and stopping them and creating better field position and taking time off the clock. And now that's come in vogue like that's the right thing to do. Well, as soon as someone houses it, then they're going to say shouldn't have done that. So not with that player back there. So anyway, not to a long answer, but yeah, it's uh it's one of those things that that after the fact, you can argue it whichever way you want to. >> This might be dipping too deep into your ongoing analytics department that you're developing, but we talk about kind of how field position has shifted with the kickoffs and you're starting closer to the the 40 a lot of times. And I'm just I'm curious. How is your evaluation of what's most important for punters changed as field position maybe has changed? >> Um yeah, I'm not going to go totally into all that. Um because I think that what there's some strategy to that. But uh yeah, I think it does change as you get closer to midfield. You know, I mean, you guys have talked about it like how far you punt the ball at from the 50 yardd line doesn't matter. it matters where you stop him um or where you give him the ball at the end of the play. Um I've talked to you guys about that when you guys talk about why did Cle Raymond return the ball um in that situation? Why did he not? Well, every yard counts. Um but I don't care if it's a two- yard return or you know, so ultimately like as you get closer to midfield, where they start with the ball is probably more important than how far or how big your net is or how far you're punting the ball or anything like that. So that would be in general as you back up further. Obviously the net is more important than the field position. Big net's going to be good field position. >> Speaking of punters, um maybe this is a more appropriate question for Bears week, but uh their punter has that kind of banana kick, I guess they call it, that's forced a couple turnovers. Just how unique is that punt and is that something that you guys can prepare for? >> Yeah, I think these guys work that stuff all the time. Fox will hit balls like that in practice, you know. Um I think anytime you're doing something like that, I think with a punter as a coach, you got to say like, "Hey, this kid, this guy likes really doing this and he's good at it and he feels comfortable and confident at it." And if it's something like that, then you would end up maybe starting to utilize that into his game. Um but these guys practice all kinds of stuff all the time. And then we'll hit our returners some of these balls throughout the course of the week just so that they're getting work on it, you know. Um I don't the only the the time I can tell you obviously the end over end punt came into play when the Aussie from the Chargers uh was a long time ago came in and started playing. he really brought the end overm punt. And then after that it went a long period of time where there was it was either a regular punt or an end overm punt. And then Baltimore um Baltimore really started to develop like multiple kicks and I I forget exactly when that was but probably in the like early 2010 11 12 somewhere in there um 13 and then Baltimore started hitting multiple kicks and that became a big you know story for Sports Illustrated whoever wrote it. Um but uh these guys have been doing that stuff now since then for years and so you see it but it obviously catches steam when you know somebody makes a play and then they say that's the reason why it happened and um but yeah so stuff like that's out there all the time. So, I just start uh briefly with um I thought it was the timing and everything of the by-week, especially with this year and what took place first few weeks of the season was outstanding. Uh and kind of the vibe and theme for the players and coaches was let's build off the positives, which there were there was a lot of those. And obviously, it's good to go into the buy coming off of the performance like we did in the Arizona game. Uh, so let's build off the positives and then let's make sure we're learning from the negative things that showed up. Um, and that was a contingency through the whole deal. Um, I thought the staff did a phenomenal job identifying certain things that we did. Um, with it being only a small sample size of games, the recollection of the plays and everything was right there. So, it didn't take us as much time as it would on a week 10 by or something like that to have the recall of what took place. But just the building, the answers, having answers, the players accountability, it all was outstanding during those by-week meetings, and we're looking to build off of that. It seemed like it was an eternity ago, and we've been we've been preparing for this big uh game this week, but I believe we'll be ready to go Sunday. >> Getting, you know, Brian Brent back before, but now that, you know, it's looking like he in line to play. Yeah. How do you envision him helping and just his role, you know, this week? whenever, you know, obviously you could gain a player like BB and his caliber back. Um, it's outstanding. You know what I mean? Uh, I don't want to start, you know, know guys, I'm not big on like giving you projections and, oh, he's going to do this, he's going to do that. Uh, it's just beautiful to have BB back. Um, there's multiple things obviously that player can do to help us. Uh, and we'll find the spots that we feel is right and he feels right for him as we progress here. >> You have to have on a snap count early. I mean, is there something, you know, when you're coming back from an Achilles, how do you incorporate him into the >> Yeah, we haven't given like a rep count or anything like that. It's going to be more of a feel thing as the game goes and we'll pick and choose, you know, what's right and what's not. >> And then on that that Arizona performance, how much do you think that Arizona performance is closer to the real, you know, you guys on defense and and how do you make sure you replicate that going forward? >> Yeah, I mean, each week is different to be honest, Davis, you know, I'm not telling you nothing you don't know. Uh, and week to week you try to do what's best for the defense and for the team success week to week. And every week's different. Every week's going to call for certain things to change. Every week's going to call for different guys needed to step up depending on where the ball is focused on and so on and so forth. So, I don't want to say we're going to replicate anything. What I want to say is I definitely want to build on a lot of the positives that came from that game. And I just want to credit the players, man. Uh, that's the thing that gets lost in all that. People start to, oh, what did you change? what did you do? But the players went out and executed and played at a high length and played at a high level like they expect to do every every week. Uh it just showed up in Arizona on a more consistent basis than it had the previous four weeks. >> I guess that's what I meant by replicate too. Not doing the exact same things defensively, but you think that's the players are now at the point where they can >> Absolutely. They definitely carry a little more swagger now when you come off a performance like that. Absolutely. >> You're going against an offense this week that that really hunts the explosives, I guess. What is just the biggest challenge of going against an offense that's big game hunting so frequently? >> Yeah, they're number one in the league when it comes to that category. Um, as far as big plays, the deep balls, uh, it's why Jordan Love is special. He has one of the best deep balls I've seen. And I mean, he flicks it 50 yards off his fingertips. Uh, it's very impressive. They have two of the most explosive vertical receivers in the game. Um, you know, it's a tremendous challenge for us. Uh, and we understand what we're going into. Uh, first division game. we're excited for it and when we'll be ready. >> The challenge of you study a team and then get a guy like Josh Jacobs back. Does that change what they do? Have they still kind of run the same concepts? Maybe just not as successful without Josh and just what's the challenge of a guy, a Pro Bowl caliber guy being inserted into the lineup and having to deal with that. >> They're probably over there just like we are about BB to be honest with you. You know what I mean? It's kind of the same for them. Everybody's asking how much is he glisten whenever you could gain a allp pro player back obviously that's going to boost everything. Everybody's just looking at the run game. It's going to open up everything. It's gonna boost everything. So it's just a matter for them just like us like how much will he do but we're prepared to play the player. We've played him previous not only Green Bay when he was in Vegas. Uh have the utmost respect for that player. Josh Jacobs I think he's one of the top end guys in this league. Uh and like I said I believe we'll be prepared for the challenge. Speaking of things to build on, just how impressed and how much more do you think Keith Abney can grow now that he's got a start at safety under his belt and just what you liked out of the rookie. >> Yep. I thought he went out and did his job and then that's and that's and that's what's important especially at that position. Um when you're the roof of the defense, things can go really bad when that player makes a mistake. Uh and that's something he's consistently did. I stood up here and told you guys dating back through training camp, he was one of the smartest rookies I ever been around. And again, credit the player, man. a player that didn't play safety since middle school and you ask him to go do that in the NFL and for him to perform the way he did, the efficiency in which he played with, but it's still so much meat left on that bone. And he'll be the first to tell you things he did in that game that he wants back that he wants to do better, but a lot more positive to build on than negative to learn from when it comes to that player. We've seen we've seen Andis play more snaps. He's the past three games, especially in those um nickel packages playing opposite Reed and he's he's played pretty well. What what have you made of his growth since his week three debut? And is there something he can do to possibly challenge for that starting quarterback spot opposite DJ Reed in the >> same things I've told you guys when it come to that cornerback room? It is just building off training camp as far as the competition. And what I say when you do that in an environment with real guys, they rise. The cream's going to rise. and credit Roger, not just not just Enus, but Roger as well. Those guys are starting to rise and as they rise, they'll create more opportunities for themselves. And it's up to them as far as what they do with it. But credit both those guys. They went out in that game and played a lot of man with no help in that game. And that's not easy to do in the NFL when you're called to do it at the frequency we ask those two to do it in Arizona. And I just want to credit them, man. and just continue to build on those things and understand let's continue to grow now. No backtracking. Let's just continue to grow. >> I know you don't want to get you don't want to get too far ahead. Sorry. You don't want to get too far ahead with any one given player after three games, but are you beginning to see the signs in of the player that you guys thought you you may have drafted back in in 2024? >> Yeah, I mean for myself personally, I've always seen the signs. Um like I said with E, the first two years has just been about availability. It wasn't necessarily like he was out there playing and losing a job or anything. He really never got his cleats in the ground and got to get settled in really because it seemed like as soon as you know he was showing and here it is, something transpired as far as the injury things that you can't control. So, I'm just happy to see him healthy, see him continuing to stack these weeks as he goes. >> Are you convinced that the shift to man coverage is best for this particular defense that you guys did in Arizona? No, I think it it it's all predicated on the game plan. Who are you playing? What's presented and what's needed like each and every week. Uh there was times in the first four weeks we played, man. And we pick and chose our spots and things like that. I'm sure you're talking about the frequency of it. Uh but no, it's just what we felt like we needed to do that week to win that football game as far as helping our team and doing our one-/3. Something that I I heard a lot in the locker room before the Arizona game and then heard a bunch after the Arizona game was those guys wanted to get back to to having fun, enjoying the game as much as doing their job and executing the scheme. How how important is it to to kind of have that free flowing mentality meshed with, you know, doing your your job schematically? >> It's ultra important, man. This game's hard enough. I tell the guys, this job and what we do is hard enough. You should get to Sunday and go out and cut it loose and have fun. And that's when I say, guys, that's kind of encompasses when I talk about it's the players. This is a players league. The coaches do the work during the week. We present them things. We show them things that we've seen. We present the plan to prepare them and try to make Monday through Saturday as stressful as possible. So, Sunday, it's easy, so to say. Now, nothing's easy in this league, but you kind of get what I'm saying. Sunday should feel free. You should go out and have fun with your brothers doing something that a small percent of this world gets blessed and fortunate enough to do. So, absolutely. And I saw that and that kind of kind of trickles into the swagger, especially on the defensive side, man. When you take the field, you want to have a bounce in your step. You want guys to feel your presence out there. But all that's built off confidence. And I think that's what you're starting to see with these guys. And I'm just excited for them, man. Because this is what I've always believed. Like I said, this is this this is what we always believe we could be and there's still so much growth and things we need to improve on moving forward off of that. >> I asked you back in I asked you back in week one about Ali McNeel and you were hesitant to say too much about him back then, but through five games, it feels like Mack is back. Just is he playing at maybe an even better level than he ever has before so far? >> Yeah, I think this is maybe the best we've seen Mack. I mean, the pressure he's creating up the middle, it's created a trickle effect for guys around him, to be honest with you. Uh, the sack total isn't even as high as the I mean, he's winning at a high rate right now and what it's doing for guys around him and how self and how selfless he is. But not only the pass rush, that's kind of what gets glamored upon, but in the run game, what he's doing in the run game and able to get back to playing stout, especially when he sees double teams and things like that. I'm just excited for him because I know the frustration he had before not being able to be him kind of his full self. >> One more on >> to Justin G. >> Yep. >> One one more on Abney. I think maybe that was a really good game to debut him just given how few deep shots the Cardinals takes. Lets him maybe see the eyes in front of him a little bit more. You got an opponent here coming here that's deep shot crazy, right? How much >> more different is that challenge for for Keith between the two opponents? How much more does he have to be wary of what's behind him with this po oonent particular? >> I think not just Keith but everybody. Everybody that takes the field against Green Bay. It's something unique that they do, you know. And credit the quarterback like everybody like he he is the superpower to the engine over there. Like he understands it, he sees it well. He feels it well. And and he trusts his guys. And that's what it come down to when you're throwing the ball 40, 50 yards down the field five, six times a game. That's trust and they do a good job at it and we have to be ready for it. The awareness to it, the detail of it and then just going to win at the catch point. That's something we've talked about because he throws it into coverage. Winning at the catch point when he does launch these deep balls. >> Sticking with the theme of of deep shots. Dan said earlier in the week that you can't necessarily just play too high against them because then you got they have a guy like Tucker Craft who will attack the middle of the field. So he he described it as like a pick your poison type of situation. And so my question is, how do you pick your voice? >> Yeah, that's that's that's you're you're trying to give the answers to the Packers here about about about what we going to do. Come on, man. You on our side here. This is But no, I know what you're getting at. Uh and then that is on coaching and understanding when to pick and choose those spots. Like the players should never have to think about that type stuff that you're talking about. That is the coach's job to make sure that we understand the down and distency, the tendencies and things like that. What have we seen? And obviously each game things change. You prepare. These coaches are good in this league and they self scout as well. So things change, but as much as you can as my job is is to make sure that I come back. Okay, I'm showing them this here. I'm showing them this here. And you know, it's a chess match the whole game. And the floor is one of the best in the business. He has one of the best offenses in the league. historically over the last what seven years and it's a reason why so we'll be ready for the challenge I believe >> back to the two games last year against the Packers and and watch film but I'm just wondering was there something that they did schematically well that that took Jir kind of out of the game plan for this team >> it's something we glance at briefly but new coordinator you know you get a little bit of feel for personnel really new coordinator on both sides of the ball so I don't think there's a ton to be gained from that standpoint So, uh, Sam Porter made some headlines yesterday just talking about his contract and everything. Um, I know you don't get into the weeds with, you know, that deal getting done, but what sort of advice have you given him? Would you give him about kind of handling this and, you know, the comments that he made publicly? >> Honestly, I didn't completely see them because, as you said, it's not part of my job, which is a benefit of my job to some extent. Um, but I think his goal is just play the best football you can and let everything else take care of itself. And I think he's done a really nice job of doing that. I'm sure it's on his mind. We're human. But, uh, when you're on the field or on the practice field, you don't even notice it. >> What is your sense of how happy or unhappy he is right now here in Detroit? >> He's been great. I mean, he's been the same person every day since the day I got here. So, uh, I I really don't notice it. >> It's kind of self-evident, but can you describe his value to everything that you guys do on offense? Obviously, you weren't here last year when he missed time, and it was pretty clear how much they did miss him. So, when you see him in the lineup, can you explain everything that he adds to the offense? It's the versatility piece. When you have a player that can do a lot of things at a high level, it becomes very difficult to defend. He's dynamic in the run game. He can block and pass pro. He can separate against linebackers and safeties. He can be a mismatch in the red zone. He can go make contested catches. He can run away from people with the ball in his hand. Uh and when you have someone that does so many of those things, well, how what are you taking away? How are you doing it? Who are you doing it with? I think it puts a lot of stress on the other side of the ball. >> These kind of comments are the kind of thing that can that spreads through wildfire in the locker room. everybody's [snorts] aware of it. How what what can you do to make sure that doesn't become a distraction for you in this game and going forward? >> Probably just do my job and move on and don't acknowledge it honestly. >> What does Kate Mazize bring to the middle of that offensive line? Obviously was playing pretty good football before the injury. Juice has played well, but you guys brought, you know, Kate in here to be the center of the future. What What does he bring to that unit? >> I think you kind of hit on it there. There's a stability factor there. He plays at a high level. He's big. He's physical. Uh he's really smart. the communication piece is a huge part of playing that position. Um, so that's just kind of a number of things off the top of my head, but excited to see him back out there. >> Two games in a row last week was Arizona. Now you go against Ganon's defense. Just how much does your knowledge and of him and what he wants to do help going into this game? >> I think there's a piece of it that helps. There's also that game theory part of it. Like he knows what I know and I know what he knows, you know? So, there's that back and forth a little bit. Plus, it's ultimately about the players. It comes down to the roster and how you utilize those guys. So, I think we're going to lean on the tape and kind of more on that aspect of things than maybe my history with him. >> What do you think I is the identity of his defense and what he wants to do? >> Yeah, he's an unbelievable coach. You know, I have a ton of respect for him as a as a coach, as a person. Um, you know, I think they do a lot they make everything look the same and they do a lot of different things and they have their foundation. They play really hard. They run to the ball. They're violent. They're tough. But I think that's kind of their calling card is that we can do a number of different things from similar looks. So, you know, you can't get a beat on what we're doing and why we're doing it. >> They also have a ton of takeaways. I think they lead the NFL in, you know, picks and and takeaways. What are they doing so well to create some of those chances? >> I think it's two things. One, when you can affect the quarterback in the pocket, you have a chance to create turnovers in the passing game, you know, and I think the other piece of it is how hard you play. Are you running the ball? Are you ripping at the ball? Do you have multiple hats of the football? And I think they do, and you see it on tape. So, we need to match that intensity the entire game. >> With the interception specifically, I mean, Goff has been really good at pro protecting the ball. So, how much do you emphasize that this week knowing that it's something he's already good at and maybe not wanting to um put too much importance on it cuz >> Yeah, I think that's probably the biggest piece. He has to go play the position with confidence. You know, I don't think a quarterback's gone through an NFL season without an interception. I could be wrong. Um at some point it may happen. Uh and that's not going to change who he is, how he plays the game. I I think it's about your process, where your eyes are, what you're seeing, what decisions you're making, and why. I think that always has to be the focus. If you start thinking about I'm not turning over, I don't want to turn it over, I think your brain starts to go to the wrong spot. >> Pretty good explosion of points in Arizona. Seven straight possessions with scores. Obviously, the slow start again, which I'm sure um irks you. And so, I'm just curious. Seems like maybe a protection breakdown a series is kind of where it's it's falling apart or run block for series. How do how do you get the offensive line to kind of calm down and and play the way that you know they're capable of playing right out the gate, Drew? Yeah, I think again it's it's emphasized, it's stressed, and at the end of the day, sometimes it's play calls, sometimes it's execution, it's always a combination of both. And and honestly, and I've said it here before, anytime we don't score, I'm a little irked whether it's the first drive of the game or the last drive of the game. Um was really excited that we got it rolling and kind of saw it in, you know, the momentum carry into the next drive and the next drive and the next drive, which was excellent. Um but kind of like the turnover piece, I also don't think you can overemphasize it because then you're putting too much pressure on it. You're paying attention to it too much. So again, it's it's doing your job. It's calling the right plays. It's staying in the moment and doing it as hard and as fast as you can. I think that's got to be the focus. >> What did you do during during the buy? I mean, what what's your kind of self- scout process when you've got those those extra few days to not have to worry about coaching a practice? >> Yeah, you hit on it. You go back and watch yourself. So, you look at different situations or, hey, are we predictable here? Do we have a tendency there? Do we like that tendency? Do we want to change that tendency? Maybe we do, maybe we don't. Uh, what are we good at? What haven't we been as good at? Do we need to emphasize things differently? do we need to emphasize something less? I think all of that goes into part of that week and then you have to put it away and get into the next opponent and kind of find where those things match so that you can put the next plan together. >> Follow a script to begin the game and how much do you deviate uh from that depending on situation how it's going. I guess what's your philosophy to kind of scripting out kind of the beginning of the game? It it's funny to say this and guys that have it changes almost week to week sometimes depending on how I feel like the game's going to be played, who we're going against, what I feel like they may do early in the game. You know, I think you you have an idea of where you want to go, certain plays you want to see come up early in the game, but that can change quickly based on, hey, we just got the ball at the plus 20 or the minus five or we ended up in second and long or second and one. You know, you kind of have those first ups in each area in your brain, but then you got to react to what's going on on the field pretty quickly. >> How many plays is your strip? Like when you >> it's like sometimes it's six, sometimes it's 12, sometimes it it it really varies based on kind of how I see the game being played and being called. >> You only use three. Do you just stay with that script then or do you >> have we have evidence at that point of what the games, you know, what's happening. So sometimes you do. You're like, "All right, we're staying on script. We're rolling." Other times you're saying, "Hey, I want to go in a different direction. Here are the three or four plays that I'm thinking about going to." And I'd say there's no, I don't know if consistency word, but there's no like repetitive nature to that aspect from the beginning of a football game. Drew, it feels like most quarterbacks are pretty dangerous in play action, but Jared's always been especially lethal. Having coached him now for five games, is there something that he does within that operation that makes him so dangerous in play action? >> I think it's a number of things. One, part of the action game is everybody. The run cell has to be there. You have to be able to run the ball. You have to have a dynamic tailback. That that definitely helps. I think just from his standpoint, one of the things that makes him so elite in that is his process. You know, it's it's uncomfortable and you don't do it a ton in college anymore where you turn your back to the defense and you have to take in a ton of information pre- snap and you have to know where your eyes need to go and who you need to locate on their side of the ball and on our side of the ball. And I think that's a huge part of the action game and it's one of the reasons you see defenses try to disguise and try to show different looks so that when you do turn your back, you're turning around and seeing a different picture. Um, and he's done it at such a high level that I think even when that happens, he's able to calibrate quickly, rig, figure out what's going on, and make the proper decision almost every time. And that's really one of the main reasons I think he's excelled in that area. >> Dan obviously likes to go for it on fourth down. What do you think the effect of those fourth down conversions against Arizona had on? I >> I think it uh you're saying like how did it affect >> I think you build confidence and a little bit of momentum and I think you put stress on them, right? high pressure situations like can we go execute? Can we make the big play? And when you do, I think you gain a little positive momentum and and when you give them up, there's that little bit of all right, you know, let's buckle up. We're still going. I think on the other side of the ball and the more that we can apply pressure to any team we're playing, the better off we're going to feel. >> Uh there was an article yesterday about what goes on in a headset, and you were quoted a couple times in that. And just kind of curious how long it took you to develop a a comfort level of what you want communication to be like on game day, and has that changed any from Arizona to Detroit? I don't know what I said. Uh I did not read the article. Uh hopefully it was well spoken and and accurate. Um I I think your headset communication is always tweaking and changing a little bit, but I think a lot of that's developed when I wasn't calling it. You know, I had I was in the NFL for 10 years before I called to play. And you I was a part of four or five different play callers, uh different systems, uh different game day processes. And I think throughout that process, you figure out what you thought went really well and other things were like, "God, that did not that would not work for me. Maybe it works for other people." And I think that's a big communication piece. It's something you talk about during preseason is a big part where you work on that. Say, "Hey, here's how I want the headset to sound." And when it gets out of line, we got to step in and get it back to where it needs to be. I think that's a huge part of coaching as a collective group that allows us to be effective. And part of that obviously starts with me of taking in the right information, asking the right questions, but then on those guys to make sure that they're doing their jobs at a high level, which they almost always are. >> You did talk about spilling Norf's coffee once upon a time. >> Oh yeah. Although it's funny, I spilled his coffee and he lost his mind. Four weeks later, he spilled his coffee. Calmst environment I've ever seen. So little bit of a double standard there. But what are you going to do? >> You've you faced uh you've faced Brian Branch as a opposing coordinator. Had to game plan for him. We've obviously seen him on the practice field this week. When when a team or defense has a safety that is that versatile and dynamic, how how difficult is that to prepare for and how aware of of him, you know, every single snap? >> It's very similar to the conversation we have about tight ends on offense. It's the versatility piece. He can cover slot receivers. He can take away tight ends. He can show up and be dynamic in the run game. And he can pressure the quarterback, you know. So, when you can do all of those different things, it's really hard to account for him because you never really know is he down there to cover, is he down there for the run, is he down there to blitz? Uh, I think when you have a guy that does that many jobs at such a high level, which is very rare, it creates that indecision for an offense of like, how much do we have to handle him? What is our ability to do that? And how much are we willing to sacrifice what we do to make sure that doesn't hurt us. One of the big uh question marks about this offensive line coming into the season was just the fact that all of these guys were playing next to somebody that they didn't play next to you the the year prior. What is I guess what have you made of the the cohesion that they've been able to develop over these first five or six weeks here? >> Yeah, it's a great question and it's a big part of playing that position and it's also the reality of the NFL. You know, that's true year to year. That's true week to week based on injuries. And the communication piece is so important. And some of that is based on reps at practice and in training camp and in preseason games. And a lot of that has to happen in the building in walkthroughs, in meetings where they're talking and asking questions. And even though it's not, hey, it's not live and it's not on the play clock. They still got to have those conversations to make sure that they're seeing the game the same way. They're anticipating things. And the communication, you know, similar to the headset conversation is what we all expect to make us all do our job at a higher level. And I think they've done a nice job of that. But it always something we're going to try to get better at. >> Drew, real quick, have you caught wind of the nickname that some of the fans have bestowed upon you so far? >> I don't know if I want to know that. [laughter] >> They're calling you Megamind. >> I wonder your reaction. I do have a big forehead.

title: VIKINGS SQUAD SHOW: Trade Rumors HEATING UP For Minnesota Vikings
text: What's up? Welcome to the Viking Squad Show. I'm Sam Extramm. Which colt would you rather have on the Minnesota Vikings? And can they just stay here? >> What's going on, Lukeman? Luke Spinman. You know, Brian Flores having an extra week to prepare for Daniel Jones. Yeah, that just doesn't seem fair. >> I'm Tyler Pisports and there was that guy who jumped on the moving school bus to save all those kids. I'm trying to figure out which Viking would be that guy. My money's on Aaron Jones. >> I'm Reggie Wilson and uh Kyler Murray, JJ McCarthy both get the start on Sunday. What world are we living in? >> Skull. It's the Viking Squad. Everything Minnesota Vikings every week. Breaking down all the big hits and gamechanging plays from the land of 10,000 lakes. the way only the Locked on Podcast Network can. It's time to gear up. The Viking Squad Show starts now. Hello, hello, hello. Happy Thursday to all. Welcome in to the Viking Squad Show on the Lockdown Podcast Network, the number one sports podcast network. Trade rumors, they are abounding about your Minnesota Vikings. They're going to be aggressive. They want Jonathan Taylor. They want Saquon Barkley. They want Patrick M. Oh well, not Patrick Mahomes, but they want a lot of guys. Um, and what will Nolan Teasley do in the next three weeks? We'll dive into all of that. Top Colts matchups of the the players that are still on the Colts and are healthy. We'll look back. Let's have do a little reminiscing on the 33 nothing comeback from four years ago. Paul Allen's 500th game coming up. We'll talk a little PA and I've got a confidence ranking activity about the Vikings depth that I'll uh I'll test the guys on. But we're brought to you today by Kelshi. Download Kelshi. Use the code locked on. Get $25 when you trade $25. Kelshi trade what's next. And speaking of trade, Luke Enman, the Vikings are connected to some heavy hitters and this Colts team that just fired its GM seems ripe for the picking. So, we've got Quinton Nelson in the mix, perhaps. Jonathan Taylor and plenty of outside options around the league as well. What name excites you most when you think about a Vikings acquisition? >> Yeah, I sat here this morning. I wrote down like 14 different names and I said, "Okay, let let's try to hone this in here a little bit." There's a lot of fun kind of expensive, maybe exciting names out there that feel like good, strong possibilities, but at the end of the day, you don't want somebody that's just exciting in October. I'm trying to think about, you know, who has the opportunity to really help this team in January and then not just January, but maybe 2027 also. So, um, I'm going back to Quint Nelson. I'm going back to Quinton Nelson. Um, I was a huge Quint Nelson guy when he came out of the draft. He has been uh everything that you could have hoped for as a uh top five pick for the Colts. I know he's getting a little long in the 230 years old, but eight time Pro Bowler, PFF's number one graded guard through these six games in 2026. Obviously, Donovan Jackson injury leaves a gaping hole. Joe Huber. Uh, commendable, you know, through through a game and a half here. And and I think we all agree we like the potential and the development we've seen from Joe Huber, but you know, you're talking about a UDFA from last year versus a perennial pro bowler. I think that's a huge upgrade. And I know we're going to get into some other positions. Running back is going to get flung out, I'm sure, by one of you three. Um, I think you start with the offensive line. You want to make your running game better, build your offensive line back up with a guy like Quinton Nelson. want to make Kyler Murray more protected and better and more ample time for deep shots to Jeff Justin Jefferson and and Jordan Addison, you build your offensive line back up. Even helps the defense. You know, if you can sustain those long drives, um, you know, whether it's through the ground or through the air, that's obviously going to keep your defense fresh as well. So, I'm going back to Quinton Nelson. I flung out a second round pick. Maybe you just start with a third round pick. You know, the Vikings do have two third round picks, so they get an extra third. They have three fifth round picks. So, two extra fifths and three sixth round picks as well. So, um you don't want to burn through all that extra capital by any means. We obviously know good rosters build through the draft, but they do have a little bit of house money to play with. And, uh if it came down to a third round pick for Quinton Nelson, even if it was just a one-year rental, uh you know, you're 5-0, you got the the world's best defense. Go add somebody on offense in the trenches like Quinton Nelson. That's what gets me excited the most. >> Yeah. Have Nelson be your left guard this year and then move Donovan Jackson to right guard. Resign Quinton Nelson because this would be the John Schneider playbook. I think I talked about this on Monday or maybe it was on a Vikings hit. >> No, it was you. You talked about >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. John Schneider. He finds players at the deadline, then he extends them and makes them part of the team's future. That would definitely be a Seattle move if they did that with Nelson. Um, and if I'm choosing like if I'm choosing one big swing to use pretty big capital on, I think I'd like to bolster the trenches. Like I think that's it's not as sexy as Jonathan Taylor, but I kind of like building up your line with someone of that caliber who's 30 years old and and hasn't shown any signs of drop off. That excites me. Forno, does that idea excite you, too? >> It does. But the one idea that really excites me isn't Nelson. And the one thing that really hesitates me with Nelson is even though he's a guard, he's kind of a cornerstone player in Indianapolis. So trading him, my my brain thinks that there's going to be a little more emotional attachment. And even though Ed Dods is the new acting general manager, he's been with Ballard the entire time. He was a a key factor in selecting Nelson. And it's not like you just have somebody come in and he they're just the interim. They've built this whole thing. So I'm very curious if that plays any factor. But I want to build the trenches on the other side of the football. I want to go for DeForest Buckner. And the reason why is very multiaceted. text: There have been several throws where the network analyst calling the game, Mark Schlareth, did this several times during the game against Cincinnati, have implored Malik just to take the check down, to take what's there. Check downs are one of them, you know, without a doubt, check downs are one of them, but you also don't want to go out there and just be throwing check downs when number one is wide open for an explosive. You know what I mean? So, like that's the nature of playing quarterback. Um and I think it all starts with just like in my mind like I got to coach this better. Like too too often right now when you watch our pass game like I just don't think everybody on the field sees the game through the same lens. And to me I kind of I I always start with me on that. Like I got to find a way to help coach this where we're all seeing the game the same way. And right now I don't think everybody all the 11 guys are seeing the game the same way. Um I think it's easy to talk about the excuse me, the quarterback, but like there's 10 other guys out there that that need to help them, you know, so you know, I I really for the most part all the way through run game and pass game like I I took a lot of time to reflect just on myself. How do I help these guys make sure we take that next step? We keep improving. I thought we have like improved in certain areas as we went through the first five weeks. This is what I would do. This is how I would approach maybe taking this away or maybe what this play like I have a hard time with this, you know. Um and that that's really valuable. Especially like you spend so much time looking at the opponent's film and and thinking through their, you know, their personnels or their structures that you have to go against but you can't always extrapolate that to how exactly we will be attacking them and uh I think a defensive head coach is able to kind of see everything and and he's able to have those conversations. Not only that, but Brian Duker is their defensive coordinator as well. >> Yeah. They're familiar with going against you know, like the bones of our offense from going against it the last few years here. Um and you get really familiar with each other schematically, also. title: Brian Fleury: "Everyone Is Very Confident In The Football Team We Have Here" | Seattle Seahawks
text: Afternoon everyone. >> How you doing? >> Great. How are you guys? >> Good. >> Fire away. >> Uh just your general assessment of the way the offense played Thursday night. >> Yeah. Um you know, I think that we improved in some certain areas where we wanted to improve. We were able to target some things that we hadn't been doing as much. We were able to feature quick game being one of them. We were a little bit more efficient there. We showed some improvement in third downs. Obviously, we didn't get the result we wanted to. So, uh, you know, everyone's disappointed with that, but I think in terms of improvement, we're still trending in the right direction. >> The two interceptions, what did you see on each of those plays? >> Yeah. Uh, you know, I'm not going to be in the habit of diagnosing plays that uh ended poorly and like pointing fingers and everything like that. There's some definitely some things we can improve on in there at all levels. Protecting the football is a is a unit objective and everybody plays a role in that. So, we'll just leave it at that. What do you feel like you guys were able to get done with this little break and assessing things and kind of whatever you need to? >> Yeah, it was awesome. You know, a lot of teams take the whole weekend off. Credit to our coaching staff. We all came in here and put in a lot of hours just kind of taking the time to look at the film from the first six games and evaluate what we're doing well at every level. Just, you know, general schematically and even at the position level and kind of highlight some things that we can lean into and focus on moving forward that will give us a better chance to succeed. On that subject, Mike had said on Monday that you felt like you guys are definitely more aligned as a team, as a group, and I'm just wondering like how you see that, what that kind of means to you. >> Yeah, 100%. I mean, anytime you've got people coming in from different places, myself with this offense, you know, there's a growth period that takes place and so Mike and I getting to know each other and then obviously getting to know all these players and trying to fit all the right pieces to the puzzle and exactly where they need to be. It's just been a process and we do feel a lot more aligned based on having the ability to have these conversations over the weekend and the direction we're going moving forward. It's going to be awesome. >> You mentioned not pointing fingers. It seems like that's a sentiment a lot of guys have shared. Do you think that's a sign that you guys are all on the same page? There's no panic involved with the offensive operation. >> Yeah, one thing that's not happening in this building is nobody's pounding the panic button because we're three and three. Everyone's very confident in the football team that we have here and we just have to continue to grow in the right direction and I think think you will see that come to fruition over the course of the rest of the season. What have you learned about being in the fire of the job through six games and actually being the one calling plays and the and the circus that that can be and kind of now that it is all on your shoulders and and now you have a chance to kind of take a weekend to reflect on it and such too. >> No, it's it's been awesome. I'm I'm happy to have been through some of these critical moments early on in the season where you've got opportunities to learn from them and get better from the quarterback situation, the running back situation, the offensive line, and then, you know, we've been in some critical moments in terms of games, too. down two scores in the second half and having to find ways to fight back and then, you know, having to manipulate or manage some of those uh end of the game drives where we're trying to get the winning score. So, I'm glad to have had all those experiences so early and uh been able to learn from them. >> Taking back taking you back a little bit this interview, you said third third down improved without the specific plays. What were those things that you saw that improve your third down? Was it was third manageable? Was it a schematic? >> We did we did have a little bit more third manageables. We put an emphasis on getting the ball out quicker because of how dynamic their pass rush was. And so we were able to execute those plays which helped us from a percentage standpoint. There's still a lot of room for growth. Don't get me wrong. We haven't like solved every issue there, but we were able to identify some things that would lead to us having more success and then we went out and executed those. >> You guys were in shotgun quite a bit in that game. Do do you look at that as just a function of, hey, that's what you had to do based on how the game was playing or do do you see that as maybe kind of a departure from what you guys like ultimately the mode you ultimately want to be in? >> Both. Yeah. Uh um I definitely leaned in that direction in the second half in hindsight maybe more than I would have preferred to just because of the confidence I have in Sam in some of those moments in order to get the ball out down the field in order to take advantage of how they were double teaming Jackson leaving Sheet and Coupe most of the time one-on-one on the opposite side. So it's just something a decision I made in the moment. Um you know there's plenty of different ways to go back and look at it. I'm always very critical of myself and there's some things I could have done differently that maybe would have helped the game play out differently, but just take it as a learning experience and move on. >> Brian, when you looked back at the first six games over the weekend, what was your evaluation of the run game and it sort of evolution through that time? >> Yeah, I there's obviously room for improvement and we've been dealing with some moving pieces there uh at a couple different places. And so, you know, there's we were able to identify some schemes and some like formation structures and movements that maybe we don't need to use as much and kind of lean into, like I said, the things that we feel like we're executing well, the blocks and the combination that we feel like the guys are executing well over and over again. We can lean more into those and hopefully gain some momentum. And then doesn't mean it was a complete departure from the other stuff, just not what we want to feature right now. What could he maybe he plays this weekend, maybe he doesn't, but what could Zach add to that if he, you know, when when he is able to finally come back? >> Yeah, I think the the great thing about Zach is everybody in the building has a comfort level with him. There's a little level of reassurance when he's out there. Whenever that happens, right, the offensive line has a lot of faith in the fact that when we're giving Zack the ball that he's going to not only hit the hole for what it for where it's supposed to be, but he's going to get generate extra yards by running through contact. And it's just like a momentum thing that I think everybody feels because of shared past experience. Not that the other guys can't do that, but there's something to be said for like doing it with somebody and you know exactly what you're getting. >> Zack's coming off obviously a serious injury. How's he kind of looked to you the last few weeks with getting ramped up in practice? >> He looks he looks great. I mean, I can't wait to get him back out there. Obviously, we're going through a process and it's not my decision exactly as to when that's going to be, but I'm excited for when that moment comes. >> You had success with using Shahid out of the back field a couple weeks ago. We haven't seen quite like that. I mean, do you feel like you still get the same thing out of that when you give him the ball on like end of rounds? So, he's when he's not lined up in the back field, but still gets it in his hands. >> Yeah. Uh, and you're referring to the red zone play down there. Yeah. Yeah.
